title: Deep Learning–Driven Chest Radiography: An Integrated Framework for Image Enhancement, Automated Diagnosis, and Fairness Optimization
abstract: Chest radiography is the most accessible and economical imaging modality for the diagnosis of pulmonary and cardiovascular diseases. However, issues, including low image quality, inter-observer variability, and demographic bias, limit the full therapeutic potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) driven interpretations. To solve these issues, the current work presents a unified deep learning system that integrates multi-stage image augmentation, automated diagnostics, and fairness optimization. The first stage employs several enhancement techniques, such as adaptive median filtering for noise suppression, Histogram Equalization (HE) using Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) for contrast refinement, and Drago's tone-mapping for brightness normalization, to improve the perceptual and diagnostic quality of chest X-rays. In the second stage, a deep learning model based on DenseNet is presented for the automated classification of thoracic illnesses. Significant data augmentation and transfer learning optimize it. In order to minimize bias and ensure parity among demographic groupings, Supervised Contrastive Learning (SCL) is integrated in the final stage. Extensive testing on benchmark datasets (NIH ChestX-ray8, CheXpert, and COVIDx) demonstrates notable increases in Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), classification accuracy, and fairness metrics when compared to current baselines. The proposed framework improves image quality from 22.37 dB to 30.45 dB PSNR and 0.65 to 0.88 SSIM, while diagnostic performance improves, achieving 92.4% accuracy and 0.937 AUC. Finally, demographic disparity measured using Demographic Parity Difference (DPD) decreases from 0.10 to 0.05.

claims.text: The proposed enhancement framework improves PSNR on NIH CXR8 from 22.37 dB to 30.45 dB compared to raw inputs.
The proposed enhancement framework improves SSIM on NIH CXR8 from 0.65 to 0.88 compared to raw inputs.
The full framework achieves 92.4% classification accuracy and 0.937 AUC on the NIH ChestX-ray8 test set.
The full framework achieves a Demographic Parity Difference (DPD) of 0.05 and Equalized Odds (EO) of 0.07 on the NIH ChestX-ray8 test set.
When trained on NIH ChestX-ray8 and tested on CheXpert without retraining, the proposed framework achieves an AUC of 0.912 compared to 0.887 for baseline DenseNet.
Intersectional fairness analysis for Female ≥60 vs. Male <40 subgroups shows DPD reduction from 0.14 to 0.06 and EO reduction from 0.17 to 0.08 after applying SCL.

The proposed framework obtains lower AUC and F1-scores for Infiltration (AUC 0.752, F1 0.609), Pneumonia (AUC 0.791, F1 0.639), Consolidation (AUC 0.812, F1 0.651), and Nodule (AUC 0.803, F1 0.658) than for visually distinct conditions.

Supervised Contrastive Learning (SCL) utilizes demographic group labels exclusively to build cross-demographic positive pairs sharing pathology labels during training, omitting sensitive attributes during inference.

limitations.text: Existing image enhancement techniques frequently process images separately without considering downstream diagnosis or fairness across patient subpopulations, leading to demographic bias in diagnostic models.
Some demographic subgroup and intersectional cohorts contain smaller sample sizes, potentially increasing variance in fairness metric estimates.
Enhancement methods such as CLAHE and tone mapping may introduce artificial intensity patterns or alter subtle image patterns if parameters are not carefully controlled.

Public datasets may contain hidden demographic, institutional, and labeling biases, rendering the findings promising but not fully conclusive for external deployment without prospective or reader study validation.

future_work.text: Explore intersectional fairness analysis (e.g., Female ≥ 60 years) to further evaluate bias across combined demographic attributes.
Conduct radiologist reader studies comparing diagnostic decisions on raw and enhanced images.
Perform multi-center validation, prospective testing, and domain adaptation to confirm real-world clinical reliability.

methodologies.name: Integrated Enhancement-Diagnosis-Fairness Framework
methodologies.description: A three-stage framework combining NAMF, CLAHE, and Drago tone mapping for enhancement, DenseNet-121 for automated multi-label thoracic disease diagnosis, and Supervised Contrastive Learning (SCL) for demographic fairness optimization.
